title: Retinal Artery Macroaneurysm (RAM): The Pulsatile Threat
summary: A focal, acquired dilation of a retinal artery, typically involving the first three orders of bifurcation. Characterized by its dramatic multi-level 'hourglass' hemorrhages and strong association with systemic hypertension in elderly patients.

sections.title: Etiology & Pathophysiology
content: 1. Chronic Hypertension: Leads to focal arteriolar wall necrosis.
2. Replacement: Muscularis layer is replaced by collagenous tissue.
3. Weakening: Loss of wall elasticity leads to fusiform or saccular dilation.
4. Dynamics: High-pressure arterial flow causes progressive enlargement.
5. Outcome: Either spontaneous thrombosis (involution) or rupture (hemorrhage).

rows: Macular edema, circinate exudates, gradual vision loss
Acute rupture of the aneurysm wall
Incidental finding on fundoscopy; 'Silver wire' appearance

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Location: Most common at arterial bifurcations or arteriovenous crossings.
The 'Hourglass' Heme: Simultaneous sub-internal limiting membrane (ILM) and sub-retinal hemorrhage.
Vascular Changes: Arteriolar narrowing distal to the RAM, focal emboli (Gunn signs).
Exudates: Often forms a 'circinate' pattern around the lesion if chronic leakage occurs.
Pulsation: Visible pulsations may be noted in the aneurysm (high risk for rupture).

rows: Early filling with late leakage/staining; masking if heme is present
Superior visualization through hemorrhage; well-defined hyperfluorescent 'bulb'
Bowed-out ILM, intraretinal fluid, or shadowing from dense blood
Used if Vitreous Hemorrhage obscures the view to rule out RD

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Step 1: Systemic Control - Immediate BP monitoring and management of dyslipidemia.
Step 2: Observation - Indicated if vision is good, RAM is distal to macula, or signs of fibrosis.
Step 3: Anti-VEGF (e.g., Ranibizumab 0.5mg or Aflibercept 2mg) - First line for macular edema.
Step 4: Laser Photocoagulation - Argon laser (200-500µm) to the lesion or surrounding 'Girdle'.
Step 5: Surgical Intervention - PPV + subretinal tPA (12.5-25µg/0.1ml) for massive submacular heme.

sections.title: Laser Photocoagulation Parameters
content: Direct Treatment: Lower energy, large spot size (500µm) directly on the RAM to induce thrombosis.
Indirect/Girdle: Two rows of confluent burns surrounding the RAM (reduces risk of rupture).
Risks: Artery occlusion, hemorrhage induction, or epiretinal membrane formation.
Preference: Currently moving toward Anti-VEGF as primary therapy for exudative RAM.

sections.title: CRITICAL RED FLAGS
content: Sudden vision loss in a hypertensive patient (Rupture/VH)
Sub-macular hemorrhage (High risk of RPE/photoreceptor toxicity within 24-48 hours)
Pulsatile Macroaneurysm (Impending rupture)
Systemic hypertensive crisis (Requires urgent medical referral)

content.explanation: R - Rupture (Hemorrhage), R - Retinal Artery (Location), R - Risk (Hypertension), R - Resolution (Spontaneous involution).

sections.title: Surgical Techniques for Submacular Heme
content: 1. Pars Plana Vitrectomy (23G or 25G).
2. Subretinal injection of tPA (Tissue Plasminogen Activator).
3. Fluid-Air exchange with prone positioning (Pneumatic displacement).
4. Intravitreal Gas tamponade (SF6 or C3F8).

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Exam High-Yields
content: RAM is almost always ARTERIAL (unlike BRVO which is venous).
The presence of a 'z-shaped' kink in the artery is often a precursor to RAM formation.
Sub-retinal blood from a RAM is more neurotoxic than sub-ILM blood.
90% of cases are UNILATERAL; if bilateral, check systemic vasculitis or severe uncontrolled HTN.

rows: Good if treated early with Anti-VEGF

sections.title: Recent Advances
sections.content: Recent small-scale studies suggest that Subthreshold Micropulse Laser (SML) may be as effective as traditional photocoagulation for exudative RAM while minimizing the risk of iatrogenic scotoma or vascular occlusion. Additionally, OCT-Angiography (OCT-A) is proving vital for non-invasive monitoring of aneurysm flow and spontaneous thrombosis without the need for repeated dye injections.
